questions.question: Who among the following is the hero of the Sanskrit historical poem, the 'Ramacharita' written by Sandhyakar Nandi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramapala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ramapala was the ruler of the Pala dynasty in Bengal.
 
• The 'Ramacharita' is a historical poem written by Sandhyakar Nandi, which praises the deeds of Ramapala.
 
• The poem highlights the achievements and valor of Ramapala, portraying him as a heroic figure.
 
• Ramapala's reign marked a significant period in the history of the Pala dynasty, often considered its last great ruler.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pala Dynasty**

 
 
• The Pala dynasty was an Indian imperial power during the Late Classical period, primarily ruling over the Bengal and Bihar regions.
 
• Founded by Gopala in the 8th century, the dynasty is known for its contributions to Buddhism and the establishment of numerous monasteries.
 
• Notable rulers include Gopala, Dharmapala, Devapala, and Ramapala, who expanded the kingdom and promoted art, culture, and learning.
 
• The Pala rulers were patrons of the famous universities of Nalanda and Vikramashila, which became renowned centers of Buddhist learning.
 
 
 
• **Sandhyakar Nandi**
 
 
• Sandhyakar Nandi was a renowned poet and scholar of the Pala court.
 
• He authored the 'Ramacharita', a historical poem that serves as a significant literary work, providing insights into the history and culture of the Pala period.
 
• The 'Ramacharita' is written in Sanskrit and is considered an important source for understanding the political and social conditions of the time.
 
• Sandhyakar Nandi's work is appreciated for its literary merit and historical value, offering a detailed account of Ramapala's reign and achievements.

questions.question: According to the Census of India 2011, which group of Union Territories recorded the highest sex ratio?

options.text: Puducherry, Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Puducherry** recorded the highest sex ratio among Union Territories in the Census of India 2011.
 
• The sex ratio in Puducherry was **1037 females per 1000 males**.
 
• **Lakshadweep** and **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** also had relatively high sex ratios.
 
• The sex ratio is an important indicator of gender balance in a region, reflecting the number of females per 1000 males.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sex Ratio**

 
 
• The sex ratio is defined as the number of females per 1000 males in a given population.
 
• It is an important demographic indicator that helps understand the gender composition of a population.
 
• A balanced sex ratio is crucial for the overall socio-economic development of a region.
 
• Factors such as sex-selective abortions, female infanticide, and differential mortality rates between genders can influence the sex ratio.
 
 
 
• **Census of India**
 
 
• The Census of India is a decennial (every ten years) exercise conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
• The census provides comprehensive data on the population, including age, sex, literacy, religion, and other demographic parameters.
 
• The Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India since 1871.
 
• Accurate census data is vital for planning and implementing various government policies and programs.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories**
 
 
• Union Territories (UTs) are regions in India that are governed directly by the Central Government.
 
• Unlike states, UTs do not have their own governments and legislatures.
 
• Examples of Union Territories include Puducherry, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, among others.
 
• The governance and administrative mechanisms in UTs are overseen by the President of India through an appointed administrator.

questions.question: Which of the following two quantities have the same dimensions?

options.text: Power and radius of circular motion

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Work and torque**__.

• **Work and torque** have the same dimensions, which is energy or force times distance.
 
• The dimension of work is given by M¹L²T⁻².
 
• The dimension of torque is also M¹L²T⁻².

questions.question: The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy devised by which of the following Governor-Generals of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Dalhousie served as the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.
 
• He is known for his aggressive expansionist policies, including the Doctrine of Lapse.
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was used to annex several Indian states into British India if the ruler died without a direct heir.
 
• Key states annexed under this policy include Satara, Jhansi, and Nagpur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Doctrine of Lapse:**

 
 
• It was an annexation policy applied by Lord Dalhousie when an Indian ruler died without a male heir.
 
• According to this doctrine, the princely state would be annexed into British India if there was no legitimate male heir.
 
• This policy led to the annexation of several states such as Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), Jhansi (1854), and Nagpur (1854).
 
• This policy was one of the factors leading to the Indian Rebellion of 1857 as it caused widespread resentment among Indian rulers and their subjects.
 
 
 
• **Lord Wellesley:**
 
 
• Lord Wellesley was the Governor-General of India from 1798 to 1805.
 
• He is known for the Subsidiary Alliance system, which was a treaty between the British East India Company and Indian princely states.
 
• Under this system, Indian rulers were not allowed to have their own armed forces and were protected by the Company in return for a subsidy.
 
 
 
• **Lord Mayo:**
 
 
• Lord Mayo served as the Viceroy of India from 1869 to 1872.
 
• He is known for his efforts in financial and administrative reforms.
 
• He was assassinated in 1872 by a convict in the Andaman Islands.
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning:**
 
 
• Lord Canning was the Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• He became the first Viceroy of India after the British Crown took over the administration from the East India Company in 1858.
 
• He is known for his efforts to calm the situation post-rebellion and implementing the Queen's Proclamation of 1858, which promised to respect the rights and dignity of Indian princes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a man-made ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aquarium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An aquarium is a human-made environment designed to house water-dwelling organisms such as fish, plants, and other aquatic animals.
 
• It is a controlled environment where the conditions such as temperature, light, and food supply are regulated by humans.
 
• Aquariums can vary in size from small glass bowls to large public aquariums that house thousands of marine species.
 
• Aquariums serve various purposes including entertainment, education, research, and conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natural Ecosystem**

 
 
• A natural ecosystem is an environment that occurs naturally without human intervention.
 
• Examples of natural ecosystems include forests, deserts, grasslands, rivers, and oceans.
 
• In natural ecosystems, the interaction between living organisms (plants, animals, and microorganisms) and non-living components (soil, water, air) occurs naturally.
 
• Natural ecosystems are self-sustaining and maintain a balance of energy and nutrient cycles.
 
 
 
• **Man-made Ecosystem**
 
 
• A man-made or artificial ecosystem is created and maintained by humans.
 
• Examples include aquariums, gardens, farms, urban parks, and reservoirs.
 
• In these ecosystems, humans control various factors such as the species present, their population, and the physical conditions.
 
• Man-made ecosystems are important for research, recreation, food production, and conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Differences between Natural and Man-made Ecosystems**
 
 
• Natural ecosystems develop through natural processes without human intervention, while man-made ecosystems are created and maintained by humans.
 
• Natural ecosystems are typically more complex and diverse compared to man-made ecosystems.
 
• Man-made ecosystems often require continuous human management and input to sustain them.
 
• Both types of ecosystems play crucial roles in supporting life and maintaining ecological balance.

questions.question: Which state government honoured Vani Jairam with the MS Subbulakshmi Award for 2019?

The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• The MS Subbulakshmi Award is named after the legendary Carnatic vocalist MS Subbulakshmi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which region in India receives less rainfall in summer, but heavy rainfall in winter season due to the retreating north easterly winds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eastern coastal region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eastern coastal region of India, particularly the Tamil Nadu coast, receives substantial rainfall during the winter months.
 
• This rainfall is primarily due to the retreating North-Easterly monsoon winds, which pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and bring it to the eastern coast.
 
• Unlike the summer monsoon, which affects the western coastal region more, the retreating monsoon impacts the eastern coast significantly.
 
• This pattern results in a unique climatic condition where the Eastern coastal region experiences less rainfall during the summer but heavy rainfall during the winter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monsoon Winds**

 
 
• Monsoon winds are seasonal winds that bring significant rainfall to parts of the world, including India.
 
• They are characterized by a reversal in wind direction and are typically divided into two main phases: the South-West Monsoon and the North-East Monsoon.
 
• The South-West Monsoon occurs from June to September and brings heavy rainfall to most parts of India.
 
• The North-East Monsoon, also known as the retreating monsoon, occurs from October to December and brings rainfall to the eastern coast of India.
 
 
 
• **Retreating Monsoon**
 
 
• The retreating monsoon refers to the period when the South-West monsoon winds start withdrawing from the Indian subcontinent.
 
• During this period, the North-East Monsoon winds take over, bringing rainfall to the eastern coast of India.
 
• This period is crucial for regions like Tamil Nadu, which receive the bulk of their annual rainfall during this time.
 
 
 
• **Bay of Bengal**
 
 
• The Bay of Bengal is the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, bounded by India, Bangladesh, and Myanmar.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the monsoon system, particularly for the North-East Monsoon.
 
• The retreating monsoon winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal, leading to significant rainfall along the eastern coast of India.

questions.question: Which of the following are the two basic categories of an ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Terrestrial and Aquatic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Terrestrial ecosystems are based on land and include forests, grasslands, deserts, and tundra.
 
• Aquatic ecosystems are water-based and are categorized into freshwater ecosystems (like rivers, lakes, and ponds) and marine ecosystems (like oceans, coral reefs, and estuaries).
 
• Both terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems have distinct flora and fauna adapted to their specific environments.
 
• These ecosystems play crucial roles in maintaining the balance of the Earth's environment through processes like the water cycle, nutrient cycling, and providing habitats for various species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terrestrial Ecosystems**

 
 
• These ecosystems are found on land and encompass a variety of biomes including forests, grasslands, deserts, and tundra.
 
• Each biome within the terrestrial ecosystem has distinct climate conditions, soil types, and plant and animal life.
 
• Forests, for instance, are dominated by trees and support a wide range of biodiversity, while deserts are characterized by low rainfall and specialized plants and animals adapted to arid conditions.
 
• Grasslands have vast open spaces dominated by grasses and are often used for agriculture and livestock grazing.
 
 
 
• **Aquatic Ecosystems**
 
 
• These ecosystems are located in bodies of water and are classified into freshwater and marine ecosystems.
 
• Freshwater ecosystems include rivers, lakes, ponds, and streams. They are home to a variety of fish, amphibians, plants, and microorganisms.
 
• Marine ecosystems include oceans, coral reefs, and estuaries and are the largest of Earth's aquatic ecosystems, covering over 70% of the Earth's surface.
 
• Marine ecosystems are incredibly diverse and are vital for global processes like carbon cycling and climate regulation.

questions.question: For which of the following states was the Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, introduced in the Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Orders (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced specifically for the state of **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• This bill aims at including or excluding certain communities from the list of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the state.
 
• The amendment is part of the government's ongoing effort to ensure that the benefits of reservation and other affirmative action policies reach the intended communities.
 
• Such amendments are periodically made based on recommendations from the state governments and after thorough evaluation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**

 
 
• Scheduled Castes are those communities that are specified in the Constitution of India under Article 341.
 
• They are often marginalized communities that have historically faced social and economic disadvantages.
 
• The constitution provides for affirmative action in the form of reservations in education, employment, and politics to uplift these communities.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**
 
 
• Scheduled Tribes are specified under Article 342 of the Constitution of India.
 
• These communities are often indigenous people who have historically been isolated from mainstream society.
 
• Affirmative action policies also apply to these communities, including reservations in various sectors.
 
 
 
• **Reservation Policies in India**
 
 
• Reservation policies are designed to improve the socio-economic status of marginalized communities by ensuring their representation in education, employment, and politics.
 
• These policies are based on the principles of social justice and affirmative action as enshrined in the Indian Constitution.
 
• Periodic revisions and amendments are made to the lists of SCs and STs to ensure that the benefits reach the deserving communities.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process for Amendments**
 
 
• Amendments to the lists of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are made through legislation passed by Parliament.
 
• State governments often recommend changes based on socio-economic studies and consultations with community leaders.
 
• Once a bill is introduced, it is discussed and passed by both houses of Parliament and then receives the President's assent to become law.

questions.question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from Irish Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• These principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, aiming to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court but the principles laid down therein are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The concept of DPSP was borrowed from the Irish Constitution, which in turn had taken the idea from the Spanish Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concurrent List**

 
 
• The Concurrent List or List-III is a list of 52 items given in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.
 
• This list includes subjects of common interest to both the Union and the State Governments, such as education, forest, trade unions, marriage, adoption, and succession.
 
• Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on the subjects mentioned in the Concurrent List.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are the basic human rights enshrined in the Constitution of India which are guaranteed to all citizens.
 
• These rights are essential for the all-around development of individuals and to maintain human dignity.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts, subject to specific restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Rule of Law**
 
 
• The concept of Rule of Law is a fundamental principle that underpins the functioning of any democratic society.
 
• It means that every citizen is subject to the law, including lawmakers themselves.
 
• It ensures that laws are applied equally and fairly, and protects individuals from arbitrary governance.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India comprises the Chief Justice and not more than _______ other Judges appointed by the President of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**33**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India consists of the Chief Justice of India and not more than 33 other Judges.
 
• These Judges are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The maximum number of Judges in the Supreme Court is defined under Article 124 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This number can be increased by Parliament through legislation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Justice of India (CJI)**

 
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary system in India.
 
• The CJI is appointed by the President of India based on seniority and other considerations.
 
• The CJI plays a crucial role in the administration of justice and is responsible for the allocation of cases and appointment of constitutional benches.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Judges**
 
 
• Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India under Article 124(2) of the Constitution of India.
 
• The appointment process involves consultation with the Chief Justice of India and other senior judges.
 
• Once appointed, judges can serve until the age of 65.
 
 
 
• **Article 124 of the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• Article 124 of the Indian Constitution deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.
 
• It outlines the appointment, tenure, and removal of Supreme Court judges.
 
• It also provides for the Parliament's power to increase the number of judges through legislation.
 
 
 
• **Parliament's Power**
 
 
• The Parliament of India has the authority to change the number of judges in the Supreme Court through legislation.
 
• This ensures that the judiciary can be expanded to meet the needs of a growing nation.
 
• The number of judges has been increased several times since the establishment of the Supreme Court to handle the increasing workload.

questions.question: Ranjana Gauhar was awarded the Padma Shri Award (2003) for her contribution to which of the following Indian dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ranjana Gauhar is an acclaimed Indian classical dancer, renowned for her expertise in the Odissi dance form.
 
• She was awarded the Padma Shri Award in 2003 for her significant contribution to Indian classical dance.
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• It is known for its intricate movements, graceful gestures, and expressive emotions, making it a distinguished art form in Indian culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance**

 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form that originated in the temples of Odisha in eastern India.
 
• It is characterized by its fluid movements, elaborate costumes, and expressive gestures.
 
• Odissi performances often depict stories from Hindu mythology, particularly the tales of Lord Krishna.
 
• The dance form emphasizes the concept of Tribhangi, the independent movement of head, chest, and pelvis.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical Indian dance form from the state of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It combines fast rhythms with fluid movements and is known for its dramatic characterization.
 
• Kuchipudi dancers are known for their dynamic footwork and impressive stage presence.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**
 
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance form from Assam, introduced by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th century.
 
• It is traditionally performed in monasteries and is known for its devotional themes.
 
• Sattriya dance is rich in mythological content and is performed with intricate hand gestures and expressions.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri**
 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form from the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• It is characterized by its graceful, gentle, and flowing movements.

questions.question: Who won the paralympic bronze medal in archery for India at Tokyo in 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harvinder Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Harvinder Singh** is the first Indian archer to win a medal at the Paralympics.
 
• He won the **bronze medal** in the men's individual recurve event at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics.
 
• Harvinder Singh defeated Kim Min Su of South Korea in a thrilling shoot-off to secure the bronze medal.
 
• His victory marked a significant achievement for India in the field of para-archery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paralympics**

 
 
• The Paralympics are a major international multi-sport event involving athletes with a range of disabilities, including impaired muscle power, impaired passive range of movement, limb deficiency, and visual impairment.
 
• The Paralympic Games are held immediately after the Olympic Games in the same host city.
 
• They are organized by the International Paralympic Committee (IPC).
 
• The Paralympics aim to highlight the achievements of athletes with disabilities and promote the values of courage, determination, inspiration, and equality.
 
 
 
• **Tokyo 2020 Paralympics**
 
 
• The Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Games were held from August 24 to September 5, 2021, after being postponed for a year due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• The Games featured 539 events across 22 sports, including athletics, swimming, wheelchair basketball, and para-archery.
 
• It was the second time Japan hosted the Paralympics, with the first being in 1964.
 
• The motto of the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics was "United by Emotion."
 
 
 
• **Para-Archery**
 
 
• Para-archery is an adaptation of archery for athletes with a range of disabilities.
 
• It has been part of the Paralympic program since the first Paralympic Games in Rome in 1960.
 
• Competitors shoot arrows at a target from a set distance, and the aim is to score as many points as possible.
 
• Para-archery events are divided into different categories based on the type and level of disability.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the composition of the agriculture sector and employment in GDP post-independence?

options.text: The proportion of employment has declined significantly but not the share of the agriculture sector in GDP.
The proportion of both the agriculture sector and employment in GDP has increased significantly.
The proportion of both the agriculture sector and employment in GDP has declined significantly.
The proportion of GDP contributed by the agricultural sector declined significantly but not the employment depending on the agriculture sector.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The proportion of GDP contributed by the agricultural sector declined significantly but not the employment depending on the agriculture sector.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Post-independence, the share of agriculture in India's GDP has seen a significant decline. This is due to the growth of the industrial and service sectors.
 
• Despite the decline in the GDP contribution, a large proportion of the Indian workforce is still dependent on agriculture for their livelihood.
 
• Structural transformation in the economy is observed where the labor force shifts from agriculture to other sectors, but this transition has been slow in India.
 
• Employment in agriculture remains high due to slow industrialization and the inability of other sectors to absorb the growing workforce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):**

 
 
• GDP is the total monetary or market value of all the finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.
 
• It serves as a comprehensive scorecard of a given country’s economic health.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture Sector:**
 
 
• This sector includes farming, fishing, and forestry, and it is a primary sector of the economy.
 
• It provides food, raw materials, and employment to a large section of the population.
 
 
 
• **Employment in Agriculture:**
 
 
• A large proportion of the workforce in developing countries like India is employed in agriculture.
 
• It includes jobs in crop production, animal husbandry, fisheries, and forestry.
 
 
 
• **Structural Transformation:**
 
 
• This refers to the shift of economic activities and labor force from agriculture to the industrial and service sectors.
 
• It is a key feature of economic development and involves changes in the structure of the economy.

questions.question: Which port is developed as a satellite port?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru Port, also known as Nhava Sheva, is the largest container port in India.
 
• Located east of Mumbai in Maharashtra, this port was developed to relieve pressure on the Mumbai Port.
 
• It was inaugurated on 26 May 1989 and named after the first Prime Minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The port is crucial for the country's shipping and logistics sector, handling a significant portion of India's containerized cargo.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ports in India**

 
 
• India has a long coastline of about 7,517 km, which is serviced by 12 major ports and over 200 non-major ports.
 
• Major ports are managed by the central government, while non-major ports are managed by state governments.
 
• Major ports handle about 60% of the country's total cargo traffic.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Satellite Ports**
 
 
• Satellite ports are developed to alleviate congestion in major ports and to enhance port capacity.
 
• They play a vital role in regional economic development and help in improving logistics efficiency.
 
• Satellite ports can be specialized for certain types of cargo, thereby streamlining operations and reducing turnaround times.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT)**
 
 
• JNPT is an autonomous corporation under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Government of India.
 
• It has state-of-the-art facilities including container terminals, liquid cargo terminals, and dry bulk cargo terminals.
 
• The port is equipped with modern technology to ensure efficient and seamless operations.
 
• JNPT has been instrumental in boosting India's trade and commerce by providing a robust infrastructure for maritime logistics.

questions.question: Which polyatomic ionic compound is a white, crystalline powder used in fire extinguishers and to neutralise acids and bases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium Bicarbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium bicarbonate, commonly known as baking soda, is a white crystalline powder that is often used as a leavening agent in baking.
 
• It is widely used in fire extinguishers due to its ability to produce carbon dioxide when heated, which helps to suffocate fires.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate can neutralize acids and bases, making it a useful compound in various chemical reactions and for pH control.
 
• It is also used in medical applications, for instance, to treat acid indigestion and heartburn by neutralizing stomach acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sodium Bisulphite:**

 
 
• Sodium bisulphite (NaHSO3) is a chemical compound commonly used as a food preservative and in the treatment of wastewater.
 
• It has reducing properties and is used in various industrial applications to prevent oxidation.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Thiosulphate:**
 
 
• Sodium thiosulphate (Na2S2O3) is an inorganic compound used in photographic processing, gold extraction, and medical treatment of cyanide poisoning.
 
• It is also used in water treatment to dechlorinate water before disposal or reuse.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Chromate:**
 
 
• Sodium chromate (Na2CrO4) is a chemical compound used in the manufacture of pigments, coatings, and other industrial applications.
 
• It is highly toxic and carcinogenic, and its use is regulated due to environmental and health concerns.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate:**
 
 
• Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) is a versatile compound with applications in baking, cleaning, fire extinguishing, and medical treatments.
 
• It is a mild base that can neutralize acids and is used in various household and industrial applications.

questions.question: Vindhyashakti was the founder of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vakataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vindhyashakti was the founder of the Vakataka dynasty, which ruled parts of central and southern India during the 3rd to 5th centuries CE.
 
• The Vakataka dynasty was contemporaneous with the Gupta Empire and played a crucial role in the politics of ancient India.
 
• They were known for their patronage of arts and culture, significantly contributing to the Ajanta Caves' development.
 
• The Vakatakas established a powerful kingdom that included regions of present-day Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Chhattisgarh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pallava Dynasty**

 
 
• The Pallavas were a significant dynasty in South India, ruling from the 3rd century to the 9th century CE.
 
• They were known for their architectural achievements, especially the rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram.
 
• The Pallava capital was Kanchipuram, which became a major center of learning and culture.
 
• The dynasty played a crucial role in the spread of Dravidian architecture and culture.
 
 
 
• **Maukhar Dynasty**
 
 
• The Maukharis were a prominent dynasty in northern India during the 6th century CE.
 
• They initially served as vassals of the Guptas before establishing their independent rule.
 
• Their kingdom included parts of present-day Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
• The Maukhari dynasty is known for its conflicts with the later Guptas and the rise of the Pushyabhuti dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty**
 
 
• The Chalukyas were an influential dynasty in southern and central India, with three distinct but related branches: the Badami Chalukyas, the Eastern Chalukyas, and the Western Chalukyas.
 
• The Badami Chalukyas ruled from the 6th to the 8th centuries CE and were known for their contributions to temple architecture.
 
• The Western Chalukyas, also known as the Kalyani Chalukyas, ruled from the 10th to the 12th centuries CE.
 
• The Eastern Chalukyas ruled in the eastern Deccan region and were known for their role in the development of Telugu culture.

questions.question: Which Indian singer wrote ‘Raag Sarita’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chintaman Raghunath Vyas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chintaman Raghunath Vyas** was a renowned classical vocalist of the Gwalior Gharana.
 
• He was born in 1924 and was popularly known as **C.R. Vyas**.
 
• He made significant contributions to Hindustani classical music and wrote several books, including **'Raag Sarita'**.
 
• C.R. Vyas was honored with prestigious awards like the **Padma Bhushan** for his contributions to Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gwalior Gharana**

 
 
• The Gwalior Gharana is one of the oldest and most prominent schools of Hindustani classical music.
 
• It was founded in the 19th century by Naththan Khan and Ustad Haddu Khan.
 
• The Gharana is known for its emphasis on precision in swara (notes) and laya (tempo).
 
• Many great maestros, including C.R. Vyas, have been associated with this Gharana.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Classical Music**
 
 
• Hindustani classical music is the traditional music of northern regions of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It has a rich history and has evolved over centuries, incorporating various elements from different cultures and eras.
 
• The music is based on ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• It includes both vocal and instrumental traditions, with prominent instruments like the sitar, tabla, and harmonium.
 
 
 
• **Padma Bhushan**
 
 
• The Padma Bhushan is the third-highest civilian award in India, established in 1954.
 
• It is awarded to individuals for distinguished service of a high order in any field, including arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• Recipients of the award are announced annually on Republic Day (26th January).
 
• C.R. Vyas received this honor for his significant contributions to Indian classical music.

questions.question: In which of the following areas did the Uprising of Khurda in 1817 take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Uprising of Khurda, also known as the Paika Rebellion, took place in the Khurda region of Odisha.
 
• It was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar, the commander of the forces of the Raja of Khurda.
 
• The rebellion was a response to the British East India Company's oppressive policies and land revenue systems.
 
• The Paikas, the traditional warrior class of Odisha, played a significant role in the uprising, showcasing their valor and resistance against British colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uprising of Khurda:**

 
 
• The Uprising of Khurda in 1817 is also known as the Paika Rebellion.
 
• The Paikas were the landed militia of Odisha, who were rendered landless by the policies of the British East India Company.
 
• The rebellion was one of the earliest organized armed rebellions against British rule in India.
 
• It was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar, who mobilized the Paikas and other sections of society against the British.
 
• The revolt was primarily a reaction to the British land revenue policies, which were exploitative and led to widespread discontent among the peasants and landed gentry.
 
• The Paikas attacked British establishments, looted the treasury, and set fire to government buildings as a mark of their protest.
 
• Though the rebellion was eventually suppressed by the British, it is remembered for its significant impact on the resistance movements against colonial rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Odisha:**
 
 
• Odisha is an eastern state of India known for its rich history, culture, and heritage.
 
• The state was known as Kalinga in ancient times and has a long history of resistance against external invasions, including that of the Maurya Empire.
 
• Odisha is famous for its temples, such as the Jagannath Temple in Puri, which is a major pilgrimage site for Hindus.
 
• The state has a diverse cultural heritage, with various traditional dance forms like Odissi, folk music, and art.
 
• Economically, Odisha is known for its mineral resources and industries, including steel, aluminum, and power generation.

questions.question: The central bank of India or Reserve Bank of India was created before Independence, in the year 1934. The recommendation to create a central bank was made by a commission called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hilton Young Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on the basis of the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• The Hilton Young Commission was set up in 1926 to review the working of the Indian currency and to suggest changes for its stabilization and better management.
 
• The Commission's report led to the enactment of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India commenced operations on April 1, 1935, as the central bank of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of the country, responsible for regulating the issue of banknotes, maintaining reserves to ensure monetary stability, and operating the currency and credit system of India.
 
• It was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• The institution is headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
 
 
 
• **Hilton Young Commission**
 
 
• The Hilton Young Commission, also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, was established in 1926.
 
• The Commission was chaired by Sir Edward Hilton Young.
 
• Its primary purpose was to examine the Indian currency system and to recommend measures for its stabilization and management.
 
• The Commission's recommendations were instrumental in the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**
 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, is the legislative framework that led to the creation of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• The Act was passed to constitute the Reserve Bank of India to regulate the issue of banknotes and the keeping of reserves to ensure monetary stability in India.
 
• It also aims to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• The Act came into force on April 1, 1935, which is when the RBI began its operations.

questions.question: Sundari trees are found in which type of forests in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mangrove forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sundari trees are the dominant species in the mangrove forests, especially in the Sundarbans.
 
• The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world and is located in the delta region of Padma, Meghna, and Brahmaputra river basins.
 
• Mangrove forests are located in coastal intertidal zones, where they thrive in saline or brackish water.
 
• Mangroves play a crucial role in coastal protection, preventing soil erosion, and supporting a diverse range of marine life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mangrove Forests:**

 
 
• Mangrove forests are unique ecosystems found at the interface between land and sea in tropical and subtropical regions.
 
• The trees in these forests have specialized root systems that help them to survive in salty and oxygen-poor soils.
 
• Mangroves provide habitat for a variety of wildlife, including fish, crabs, and birds.
 
• They act as natural barriers against storm surges and coastal erosion, thus protecting inland areas.
 
 
 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests:**
 
 
• Tropical deciduous forests are characterized by trees that shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve water.
 
• These forests receive moderate rainfall and have a rich biodiversity, including species like teak, sal, and bamboo.
 
• They are found in regions with distinct wet and dry seasons.
 
• Such forests are crucial for timber production and support a variety of wildlife.
 
 
 
• **The Thorn Forests and Scrubs:**
 
 
• Thorn forests and scrublands are found in arid and semi-arid regions where the climate is hot and dry.
 
• Vegetation is typically sparse, consisting of hardy plants like cacti, acacia, and thorny bushes.
 
• These ecosystems are adapted to conserve water and withstand prolonged drought conditions.
 
• They are important for preventing desertification and providing habitat for drought-resistant species.
 
 
 
• **Tropical Evergreen Forests:**
 
 
• Tropical evergreen forests are found in regions with high rainfall and no significant dry season.
 
• These forests are characterized by dense canopies, high biodiversity, and evergreen trees that do not shed their leaves.
 
• They are vital for carbon sequestration and maintaining global ecological balance.
 
• Some of the world's most diverse and complex ecosystems are tropical evergreen forests.
